law_name: Climate Act (lov om klima), Act No. 965 of 26 June 2020 (bill L 117, 2019–20)
description: Adopted on 18 June 2020 by 90 votes to 5, implementing an agreement between the Frederiksen I government and seven other parties. It sets a binding target of a 70% cut in greenhouse-gas emissions by 2030 compared with 1990 and climate neutrality by 2050 at the latest, requires five-yearly interim targets and climate action plans, attaches a duty to act to the targets and strengthens the independent Council on Climate Change (Klimarådet).
significance: The framework for Danish climate policy since 2020. In its 2026 status report the Klimarådet concluded that the government's policies no longer demonstrate that the 70% target will be met.

law_name: Right to early retirement (tidlig pension, 'Arne-pension'), Act No. 2202 of 29 December 2020 (bill L 104, 2020–21)
description: Implements the agreement of 10 October 2020 between the government, the Danish People's Party, SF and the Red–Green Alliance. People with 42, 43 or 44 years on the labour market by six years before the state pension age may retire one, two or three years early on a public benefit. Adopted on 21 December 2020 by 54 votes to 43 (Venstre, the Social Liberals, the Conservatives, New Right and Liberal Alliance against); in force from 1 January 2022.
significance: Delivered the Social Democrats' central 2019 campaign pledge, named after brewery worker Arne Juhl.

law_name: Transfer of asylum seekers to third countries, Act No. 1191 of 8 June 2021 (bill L 226, 2020–21)
description: Amends the Aliens Act so that Denmark can, under an agreement with a non-EU country, transfer asylum seekers there for their claims to be examined and for any subsequent protection. Adopted on 3 June 2021 by 70 votes to 24 (SF, the Social Liberals, the Red–Green Alliance and the Alternative against); the minister decides when it enters into force.
significance: Criticised by the UN and the European Commission, which said external processing was not possible under EU rules. No transfers under the law were reported in the sources consulted, and in June 2026 the new government said it would keep working to establish reception centres outside Europe.

law_name: Minimum staffing ratios in day care (minimumsnormeringer), Act No. 2594 of 28 December 2021 (bill L 92 A, 2021–22)
description: Requires municipalities to ensure a statutory minimum staffing level in municipal, independent and contracted day-care institutions and strengthens supervision, following the agreement on minimum staffing ratios of 5 December 2020 between the government, the Social Liberals, SF, the Red–Green Alliance and the Alternative. Adopted on 21 December 2021 by 78 votes to 11, with the Danish People's Party abstaining. A separate law (L 200, adopted 3 June 2021) improved the data used to monitor staffing.
significance: Made staffing ratios in nurseries and kindergartens a legal obligation rather than a policy goal.

law_name: National compromise on Danish security policy and referendum abolishing the EU defence opt-out (2022)
description: On 6 March 2022, after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Frederiksen signed with the leaders of Venstre, SF, the Social Liberals and the Conservatives a national compromise to raise defence and security spending permanently to 2% of GDP by the end of 2033 and to hold a referendum on abolishing Denmark's EU defence opt-out. In the referendum of 1 June 2022, 1,848,242 voters (66.9% of valid votes) voted to abolish the opt-out and 915,717 against, on a turnout of 65.8%.
significance: Ended Denmark's EU defence opt-out, so that it takes part in the EU's common security and defence policy; the 2% spending deadline was later brought forward to 2030.

law_name: Abolition of Store Bededag as a public holiday, Act No. 214 of 6 March 2023 (bill L 13, 2022–23, 2nd session)
description: Turns Store Bededag (the fourth Friday after Easter) into an ordinary working day from 2024, with a pay supplement of 0.45% of annual salary for salaried employees, to fund higher defence spending. Adopted on 28 February 2023 by 95 votes (S, V, M, RV) to 68.
significance: One of the most contested decisions of the SVM government (see polemics). The Frederiksen III government's legislative programme for 2026–27 announces a bill to reinstate the holiday from 2030.

law_name: Ban on improper treatment of writings of significant religious importance, Act No. 1554 of 12 December 2023 (bill L 65, 2023–24)
description: Adds a section 110 e(2) to the Criminal Code making it an offence to treat improperly, in public or with intent to spread it widely, a writing of significant religious importance to a religious community, or an object appearing to be one. Adopted on 7 December 2023 by 94 votes (S, V, M, RV and one independent) to 77 (all other parties). An earlier, broader bill (L 133, 2022–23) covering objects of religious significance lapsed.
significance: Adopted by a narrow majority, 94 to 77: the government parties and the Social Liberals for, all other parties against.

law_name: Personal income tax reform, Act No. 482 of 22 May 2024 (bill L 138, 2023–24)
description: Implements parts of the agreement of 14 December 2023 between the SVM government, the Denmark Democrats, the Conservatives, the Social Liberals and New Right: the top-tax rate is cut by 7.5 percentage points on incomes up to DKK 750,000 (2023 level) and raised by 5 points on incomes above DKK 2.5 million, the employment allowance is increased (with extra allowances for single parents and for seniors close to pension age), and inheritance-tax thresholds are changed. Adopted on 16 May 2024 by 76 votes to 30.
significance: The main tax reform of the SVM government; the reduced band is often called the 'middle tax' (mellemskat), a term the tax minister used again in October 2026.

law_name: University reform: 75-ECTS master's degrees and new professional master's programmes, Act No. 754 of 20 June 2025 (bill L 172, 2024–25)
description: Allows universities to offer master's programmes of 75 ECTS points (about one and a quarter years) and flexible 'erhvervskandidat' programmes of 75 or 120 ECTS, phasing out the one-year academic top-up degrees. Follows the framework agreement of 27 June 2023 between the government, SF, the Denmark Democrats, Liberal Alliance and the Conservatives. Adopted on 27 May 2025 by 92 votes to 16.
significance: A scaled-down version of Frederiksen's September 2022 proposal to cut about half of all master's degrees to one year.

law_name: Full gender equality in conscription, Act No. 715 of 20 June 2025 (bill L 221, 2024–25)
description: Implements part of the 2024–2033 defence agreement: women turning 18 on or after 1 July 2025 must attend Defence Day and draw a lottery number, and can be ordered to serve on the same terms as men if there are not enough volunteers; conscript sergeants and lieutenants are reintroduced. Adopted unanimously on 11 June 2025 (108 votes to 0).
significance: Adopted without votes against, as part of the defence build-up under the 2024–2033 defence agreement.

law_name: Expulsion reform (udvisningsreform), Act No. 766 of 8 September 2026 (bill L 17 A, 2025–26, 2nd session)
description: Foreign nationals sentenced to at least one year's unconditional imprisonment for certain serious crimes (including serious violence, sexual offences, organised crime, people smuggling and drug crime) are as a rule to be expelled unless very special considerations decisively weigh against it; GPS ankle-tag monitoring is introduced for foreigners punished for ten or more breaches of their reporting obligations. Adopted on 3 September 2026 by 100 votes to 10 (Red–Green Alliance and the Alternative).
significance: Delivers a pledge the Frederiksen III government made when it took office in June 2026.

law_name: Agreement between Greenland, Denmark and the United States on defence and security (signed 22 September 2026)
description: Signed at the UN in New York by Frederiksen, Greenland's premier Jens-Frederik Nielsen and US President Donald Trump. According to the BBC it amends the 1951 defence agreement, allows the US to establish additional defence areas at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig and to modernise Pituffik Space Base, bars non-NATO states from military installations in Greenland, and recognises the Kingdom's sovereignty and territorial integrity and Greenland's right to self-determination. It must still go through parliamentary procedures in Denmark and Greenland to enter into force.
significance: Ended more than a year of tension over Trump's demands to acquire Greenland; not in force as of October 2026.
